findings.title: Concurrent inserts can bypass the row ceiling
findings.description: The trades route counts rows and then fetches them in separate statements, but the pooled connection does not set a repeatable-read isolation level. Under PostgreSQL’s default READ COMMITTED isolation, a concurrent insert between those statements can make the fetch return more than `max_rows`, even though the count passed admission. The candles route has the same count-then-fetch pattern at lines 112–119. This makes the configured response-size ceiling unreliable during concurrent collection; use a consistent snapshot or another approach that enforces the limit without silently truncating results.

findings.title: Trades watermark is documented as the newest stored trade
findings.description: The `tape_complete_through` description says it is the “Created time of the newest stored trade,” but the route populates it from the trades sync watermark. That watermark represents the end of the last fully walked window, not necessarily the timestamp of any stored trade. Clients relying on the response description could misinterpret a window-completeness watermark as a trade timestamp.
